---
title: Ingest events published from a contract
description: Use Stellar RPC's getEvents method to query contract events and store them beyond the RPC retention window
---

Stellar RPC provides a [`getEvents` method] which allows you to query events from a smart contract. However, an RPC keeps events only for a limited window of recent ledgers. Each RPC operator sets this window with the `history-retention-window` setting. The default is 120960 ledgers, about 7 days. The [`getHealth` method] returns the window and the oldest ledger that a given RPC serves. If you need access to a longer-lived record of these events you'll want to "ingest" the events as they are published, maintaining your own record or database as events are ingested.

There are many strategies you can use to ingest and keep the events published by a smart contract. Among the simplest might be using a community-developed tool such as [Mercury](https://mercurydata.app) which will take all the infrastructure work off your plate for a low subscription fee. Or, [indexers](/docs/data/indexers) can provide ingested event data for affordable prices.

Another approach we'll explore here is using a cron job to query Stellar RPC periodically and store the relevant events in a locally stored SQLite database. We are going to use an Object Relational Mapper (ORM), allowing us to write database query directly in JavaScript, Python, or Go. In Java, we use plain JDBC instead.

## Setup

<Tabs>
<Tab title="Python">

In a [virtual environment](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/venv.html), install the Python dependencies:

```sh
pip install sqlalchemy stellar-sdk
```

</Tab>
<Tab title="Go">

Create a Go module (Go 1.25 or later) and install the dependencies:

```sh
go mod init ingest-events
go get github.com/stellar/go-stellar-sdk gorm.io/gorm gorm.io/driver/sqlite
```

The `gorm.io/driver/sqlite` driver uses cgo, so it needs a C compiler such as `gcc`.

</Tab>
<Tab title="Java">

Create a Maven project (Java 17 or later) and add the Stellar SDK and the SQLite JDBC driver to the `<dependencies>` section of its `pom.xml`:

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>network.lightsail</groupId>
  <artifactId>stellar-sdk</artifactId>
  <version>6.0.0</version>
</dependency>
<dependency>
  <groupId>org.xerial</groupId>
  <artifactId>sqlite-jdbc</artifactId>
  <version>3.54.1.0</version>
</dependency>
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Setup the Database Client

<Tabs>
<Tab title="JavaScript">

The finer details of choosing a Prisma configuration are beyond the scope of this document. You can get a lot more information in the [Prisma quickstart](https://www.prisma.io/docs/getting-started/quickstart). Here is our Prisma schema's model:

```text
model StellarEvent {
  id          String @id
  type        String
  ledger      Int
  contract_id String
  topic_1     String?
  topic_2     String?
  topic_3     String?
  topic_4     String?
  value       String
}
```

</Tab>
<Tab title="Python">

To access the database, we will use [SQLAlchemy](https://www.sqlalchemy.org), which is a frequently used Python library to query database.

We are going to ingest events in a table named `StellarEvent`. In SQLAlchemy, this translates into a class, also called a database model:

```python
from typing import Any
from sqlalchemy import orm, JSON


class Base(orm.DeclarativeBase):
    # needed to tell SQLAlchemy to translate a dictionary into a JSON entry
    type_annotation_map = {
        dict[str, Any]: JSON,
    }


class Event(Base):
    __tablename__ = "StellarEvent"

    id: orm.Mapped[int] = orm.mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    contract_id: orm.Mapped[str]
    ledger: orm.Mapped[int]
    topics: orm.Mapped[dict[str, Any]]
    value: orm.Mapped[str]
```

We will use an in-memory-only SQLite database for this guide, but thanks to the use of an ORM, we could be using any other supported database. We would simply need to change the connection string.

```python
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
engine = create_engine("sqlite://", echo=True)

# the following creates the table in the DB
Base.metadata.create_all(engine)
```

<Tip>

By setting `echo=True` we can understand what is happening on the database. Creating the database table leads to the following logs:

</Tip>

```text
BEGIN (implicit)
PRAGMA main.table_info("StellarEvent")
...
PRAGMA temp.table_info("StellarEvent")
...
CREATE TABLE StellarEvent (
	id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    contract_id VARCHAR NOT NULL,
    ledger INTEGER NOT NULL,
	topics JSON NOT NULL,
	value VARCHAR NOT NULL,
	PRIMARY KEY (id)
)
...
COMMIT
```

</Tab>
<Tab title="Go">

To access the database, we will use [GORM](https://gorm.io), a frequently used Go ORM. Our model is a struct with the same fields as the Prisma model. A topic field is empty when the event has fewer topics.

The Go snippets on this page are parts of one `main` package. Merge their imports into one block.

```go
package main

import (
  "gorm.io/driver/sqlite"
  "gorm.io/gorm"
  "gorm.io/gorm/logger"
)

type StellarEvent struct {
  ID         string `gorm:"primaryKey"`
  Type       string
  Ledger     int32
  ContractID string
  Topic1     string
  Topic2     string
  Topic3     string
  Topic4     string
  Value      string
}

func openDB() (*gorm.DB, error) {
  // An in-memory-only SQLite database. logger.Info prints every SQL statement.
  db, err := gorm.Open(sqlite.Open("file::memory:?cache=shared"), &gorm.Config{
    Logger: logger.Default.LogMode(logger.Info),
  })
  if err != nil {
    return nil, err
  }

  // the following creates the table in the DB
  if err := db.AutoMigrate(&StellarEvent{}); err != nil {
    return nil, err
  }
  return db, nil
}
```

As with SQLAlchemy, another supported database only needs a different driver and connection string.

</Tab>
<Tab title="Java">

To access the database, we will use plain [JDBC](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.sql/java/sql/package-summary.html) with the SQLite driver. Our table has the same columns as the Prisma model. A topic column is `NULL` when the event has fewer topics.

The Java snippets on this page are methods of one `IngestEvents` class. Merge their imports into one block.

```java
import java.sql.Connection;
import java.sql.DriverManager;
import java.sql.SQLException;
import java.sql.Statement;

public class IngestEvents {
  static Connection openDB() throws SQLException {
    // An in-memory-only SQLite database. It lives as long as this connection.
    Connection db = DriverManager.getConnection("jdbc:sqlite::memory:");

    // the following creates the table in the DB
    try (Statement statement = db.createStatement()) {
      statement.execute(
        "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS StellarEvent ("
          + "id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, "
          + "type TEXT NOT NULL, "
          + "ledger INTEGER NOT NULL, "
          + "contract_id TEXT NOT NULL, "
          + "topic_1 TEXT, topic_2 TEXT, topic_3 TEXT, topic_4 TEXT, "
          + "value TEXT NOT NULL)");
    }
    return db;
  }
}
```

As with SQLAlchemy, another database only needs a different JDBC driver and connection string.

</Tab>
</Tabs>

<Info>

Using a database model is very convenient as it allows us to control the database schema programmatically. If we need to change the schema, by adding a new columns for instance, then using an ORM allows us to use very powerful migration tools.

</Info>

We'll use this model to create and query for the events stored in our database.

## Query Events from Stellar RPC

First, we'll need to query the events from Stellar RPC. This simple example makes an RPC request using the [`getEvents` method], filtering for all `transfer` events that are emitted by the native XLM contract.

<Note>

We are making some assumptions here. We'll assume that your contract sees enough activity, and that you are querying for events frequently enough that you aren't in danger of needing to figure out the oldest ledger Stellar RPC is aware of. The approach we're taking is to find the largest (most recent) ledger sequence number in the database and query for events starting there. Your use-case may require some logic to determine what the latest ledger is, and what the oldest ledger available is, etc.

</Note>
<Tabs>
<Tab title="JavaScript">

We use the `@stellar/stellar-sdk` library:

```javascript
import { Server } from "@stellar/stellar-sdk/rpc";
import { PrismaClient } from "@prisma/client";

const server = new Server("https://soroban-testnet.stellar.org");
const prisma = new PrismaClient();

let latestEventIngested = await prisma.stellarEvent.findFirst({
  orderBy: [
    {
      ledger: "desc",
    },
  ],
});

let { events } = await server.getEvents({
  startLedger: latestEventIngested.ledger,
  filters: [
    {
      type: "contract",
      contractIds: ["CDLZFC3SYJYDZT7K67VZ75HPJVIEUVNIXF47ZG2FB2RMQQVU2HHGCYSC"],
      topics: [["AAAADwAAAAh0cmFuc2Zlcg==", "*", "*", "*"]],
    },
  ],
});
```

</Tab>
<Tab title="Python">

If we start from scratch, there is no known ledger, so we start near the oldest ledger the RPC still keeps. `get_health()` returns it. The window moves forward with every new ledger, and `getEvents` rejects a start ledger outside it, so we add a small margin.

```python
import stellar_sdk

soroban_server = stellar_sdk.SorobanServer("https://soroban-testnet.stellar.org")
ledger = soroban_server.get_health().oldest_ledger + 10
```

Later on, we will be able to start from the latest ingested ledger by making a query to our DB.

```python
with orm.Session(engine) as session:
    stmt = sqlalchemy.select(Event.ledger).where(
        Event.contract_id == contract_id
    ).order_by(Event.ledger.desc())
    ingested_ledger = session.scalars(stmt).first()

    if ingested_ledger:
      ledger = ingested_ledger
```

Let's get events from Stellar RPC!

```python
from stellar_sdk.soroban_rpc import EventFilter, EventFilterType

contract_id = "CDLZFC3SYJYDZT7K67VZ75HPJVIEUVNIXF47ZG2FB2RMQQVU2HHGCYSC"

res = soroban_server.get_events(
    ledger,
    filters=[
        EventFilter(
            type=EventFilterType.CONTRACT,
            contract_ids=[contract_id],
            topics=[["AAAADwAAAAh0cmFuc2Zlcg==", "*", "*", "*"]],
        )
    ],
)
events = res.events
```

</Tab>
<Tab title="Go">

We start from the latest ingested ledger. If the database is empty, we start near the oldest ledger the RPC still keeps, which `GetHealth` returns. The window moves forward with every new ledger, and `getEvents` rejects a start ledger outside it, so we add a small margin.

The topic filter takes the same base64 strings as the other examples, so we decode it from JSON.

```go
import (
  "context"
  "encoding/json"
  "errors"

  "gorm.io/gorm"

  client "github.com/stellar/go-stellar-sdk/clients/rpcclient"
  protocol "github.com/stellar/go-stellar-sdk/protocols/rpc"
)

const contractID = "CDLZFC3SYJYDZT7K67VZ75HPJVIEUVNIXF47ZG2FB2RMQQVU2HHGCYSC"

func fetchEvents(ctx context.Context, db *gorm.DB) ([]protocol.EventInfo, error) {
  server := client.NewClient("https://soroban-testnet.stellar.org", nil)

  var ledger uint32
  var latestEventIngested StellarEvent
  err := db.Where("contract_id = ?", contractID).Order("ledger desc").First(&latestEventIngested).Error
  switch {
  case err == nil:
    ledger = uint32(latestEventIngested.Ledger)
  case errors.Is(err, gorm.ErrRecordNotFound):
    health, err := server.GetHealth(ctx)
    if err != nil {
      return nil, err
    }
    ledger = health.OldestLedger + 10
  default:
    return nil, err
  }

  // `transfer`, then any three topics
  var topics protocol.TopicFilter
  err = json.Unmarshal([]byte(`["AAAADwAAAAh0cmFuc2Zlcg==", "*", "*", "*"]`), &topics)
  if err != nil {
    return nil, err
  }

  response, err := server.GetEvents(ctx, protocol.GetEventsRequest{
    StartLedger: ledger,
    Filters: []protocol.EventFilter{
      {
        EventType:   protocol.EventTypeSet{protocol.EventTypeContract: nil},
        ContractIDs: []string{contractID},
        Topics:      []protocol.TopicFilter{topics},
      },
    },
  })
  if err != nil {
    return nil, err
  }
  return response.Events, nil
}
```

</Tab>
<Tab title="Java">

We start from the latest ingested ledger. If the database is empty, we start near the oldest ledger the RPC still keeps, which `getHealth()` returns. The window moves forward with every new ledger, and `getEvents` rejects a start ledger outside it, so we add a small margin.

```java
import java.sql.Connection;
import java.sql.PreparedStatement;
import java.sql.ResultSet;
import java.sql.SQLException;
import java.util.List;

import org.stellar.sdk.SorobanServer;
import org.stellar.sdk.requests.sorobanrpc.EventFilterType;
import org.stellar.sdk.requests.sorobanrpc.GetEventsRequest;
import org.stellar.sdk.responses.sorobanrpc.GetEventsResponse;

static final String contractId = "CDLZFC3SYJYDZT7K67VZ75HPJVIEUVNIXF47ZG2FB2RMQQVU2HHGCYSC";

static List<GetEventsResponse.EventInfo> fetchEvents(Connection db) throws SQLException {
  SorobanServer server = new SorobanServer("https://soroban-testnet.stellar.org");

  long ledger;
  try (PreparedStatement query = db.prepareStatement(
      "SELECT ledger FROM StellarEvent WHERE contract_id = ? ORDER BY ledger DESC LIMIT 1")) {
    query.setString(1, contractId);
    try (ResultSet row = query.executeQuery()) {
      if (row.next()) {
        ledger = row.getLong("ledger");
      } else {
        ledger = server.getHealth().getOldestLedger() + 10;
      }
    }
  }

  GetEventsRequest request = GetEventsRequest.builder()
    .startLedger(ledger)
    .filters(List.of(GetEventsRequest.EventFilter.builder()
      .type(EventFilterType.CONTRACT)
      .contractIds(List.of(contractId))
      // `transfer`, then any three topics
      .topics(List.of(List.of("AAAADwAAAAh0cmFuc2Zlcg==", "*", "*", "*")))
      .build()))
    .build();
  return server.getEvents(request).getEvents();
}
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Store Events in the Database

Now, we'll check if the `events` object contains any new events we should store, and we do exactly that. We're storing the event's topics and values as base64-encoded strings here, but you could decode the necessary topics and values into the appropriate data types for your use-case.

<Tabs>
<Tab title="JavaScript">

```javascript
if (events?.length) {
  events.forEach(async (event) => {
    await prisma.stellarEvent.create({
      data: {
        id: event.id,
        type: event.type,
        ledger: event.ledger,
        contract_id: event.contractId!.toString(),
        topic_1: event.topic[0]?.toXDR('base64') || null,
        topic_2: event.topic[1]?.toXDR('base64') || null,
        topic_3: event.topic[2]?.toXDR('base64') || null,
        topic_4: event.topic[3]?.toXDR('base64') || null,
        value: event.value.toXDR('base64')
      },
    });
  });
}
```

</Tab>
<Tab title="Python">

<Tip>

Make your life easier with a SQLAlchemy [`sessionmaker`](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/session_basics.html#using-a-sessionmaker) when making transactions (e.g. add more than one record in a single database call.)

</Tip>

```python
import sqlalchemy
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker

Session = sessionmaker(engine)
with Session.begin() as session:
    events_ = []
    for event in events:
        topic_ = event.topic
        events_.append(Event(contract_id=contract_id, ledger=event.ledger, topics=topic_, value=event.value))
    session.add_all(events_)
```

```text
BEGIN (implicit)
INFO sqlalchemy.engine.Engine COMMIT
INFO sqlalchemy.engine.Engine BEGIN (implicit)
INFO sqlalchemy.engine.Engine INSERT INTO "StellarEvent" (contract_id, ledger, topics, value) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?) RETURNING id
INFO sqlalchemy.engine.Engine [...] ('CDLZFC3SYJYDZT7K67VZ75HPJVIEUVNIXF47ZG2FB2RMQQVU2HHGCYSC', 3311, '["AAAADwAAAAh0cmFuc2Zlcg==", "AAAAEgAAAAAAAAAAJY16rJOcKxQayCR7ayNA80hW5q1U4ypIGOY7NktBfKU=", "AAAAEgAAAAHXkotywnA8z+r365/0701QSlWouXn8m0UOoshCtNHOYQ==", "AAAADgAAAAZuYXRpdmUAAA=="]', 'AAAACgAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAGQ=')

...
COMMIT
```

</Tab>
<Tab title="Go">

GORM writes a slice of records in one transaction. Each run starts again at the latest ingested ledger, so we skip events that are already stored.

```go
import (
  "gorm.io/gorm"
  "gorm.io/gorm/clause"

  protocol "github.com/stellar/go-stellar-sdk/protocols/rpc"
)

func storeEvents(db *gorm.DB, events []protocol.EventInfo) error {
  if len(events) == 0 {
    return nil
  }

  records := make([]StellarEvent, 0, len(events))
  for _, event := range events {
    topic := func(i int) string {
      if i < len(event.TopicXDR) {
        return event.TopicXDR[i]
      }
      return ""
    }
    records = append(records, StellarEvent{
      ID:         event.ID,
      Type:       event.EventType,
      Ledger:     event.Ledger,
      ContractID: event.ContractID,
      Topic1:     topic(0),
      Topic2:     topic(1),
      Topic3:     topic(2),
      Topic4:     topic(3),
      Value:      event.ValueXDR,
    })
  }

  return db.Clauses(clause.OnConflict{DoNothing: true}).Create(&records).Error
}
```

Then `main` puts the steps together:

```go
import (
  "context"
  "log"
)

func main() {
  ctx := context.Background()
  db, err := openDB()
  if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
  }
  events, err := fetchEvents(ctx, db)
  if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
  }
  if err := storeEvents(db, events); err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
  }
}
```

</Tab>
<Tab title="Java">

We write all records in one transaction. Each run starts again at the latest ingested ledger, so `INSERT OR IGNORE` skips events that are already stored.

```java
import java.sql.Connection;
import java.sql.PreparedStatement;
import java.sql.SQLException;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Locale;

import org.stellar.sdk.responses.sorobanrpc.GetEventsResponse;

static void storeEvents(Connection db, List<GetEventsResponse.EventInfo> events)
    throws SQLException {
  if (events == null || events.isEmpty()) {
    return;
  }

  String sql = "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO StellarEvent "
    + "(id, type, ledger, contract_id, topic_1, topic_2, topic_3, topic_4, value) "
    + "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)";
  db.setAutoCommit(false);
  try (PreparedStatement insert = db.prepareStatement(sql)) {
    for (GetEventsResponse.EventInfo event : events) {
      List<String> topics = event.getTopic();
      insert.setString(1, event.getId());
      insert.setString(2, event.getType().name().toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT)); // "contract"
      insert.setLong(3, event.getLedger());
      insert.setString(4, event.getContractId());
      for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
        insert.setString(5 + i, i < topics.size() ? topics.get(i) : null);
      }
      insert.setString(9, event.getValue());
      insert.addBatch();
    }
    insert.executeBatch();
    db.commit();
  } catch (SQLException e) {
    db.rollback();
    throw e;
  } finally {
    db.setAutoCommit(true);
  }
}
```

Then `main` puts the steps together:

```java
import java.sql.Connection;
import java.sql.SQLException;
import java.util.List;

import org.stellar.sdk.responses.sorobanrpc.GetEventsResponse;

public static void main(String[] args) throws SQLException {
  try (Connection db = openDB()) {
    List<GetEventsResponse.EventInfo> events = fetchEvents(db);
    storeEvents(db, events);
  }
}
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Run the Script with Cron

A cron entry is an excellent way to automate this script to gather and ingest events every so often. You could configure this script to run as (in)frequently as you want or need. This example would run the script every 24 hours at 1:14 pm:

<Tabs>
<Tab title="JavaScript">

```sh
14 13 * * * node /absolute/path/to/script.js
```

</Tab>
<Tab title="Python">

```sh
14 13 * * * python /absolute/path/to/script.py
```

</Tab>
<Tab title="Go">

Build the program once with `go build -o ingest-events`, then run the binary:

```sh
14 13 * * * /absolute/path/to/ingest-events
```

</Tab>
<Tab title="Java">

Package the program once as a runnable JAR that holds its dependencies (for example, with the Maven Shade plugin), then run the JAR:

```sh
14 13 * * * java -jar /absolute/path/to/ingest-events.jar
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

Here's another example that will run the script every 30 minutes:

<Tabs>
<Tab title="JavaScript">

```sh
30 * * * * node /absolute/path/to/script.js
```

</Tab>
<Tab title="Python">

```sh
30 * * * * python /absolute/path/to/script.py
```

</Tab>
<Tab title="Go">

```sh
30 * * * * /absolute/path/to/ingest-events
```

</Tab>
<Tab title="Java">

```sh
30 * * * * java -jar /absolute/path/to/ingest-events.jar
```

</Tab>
